tone.how: Inside the plate the tone is the real low frequency difference of the plate and the hold, taken over open sea only (blue minus red in code values, no cloud), so from far up the plate carries the sea of the hold and the dark sea round the glint, a look of the low view, comes in with nearness. share is how much open sea the window must hold before the difference is trusted.

fine.how: The deepest level is the plate brought to its raster with the detail of the lay back of the close image added where the plate is that lay back: where plate and lay back, both from the 12 degree raster, are no further apart than apart (code values, after a blur of sigmaDeg), inside the close image by edgeDeg, and where the image has at least sharp image px per level px.

strip.how: A level whose window reaches past the kept level of the hold is filled there from the level above, so that reduced to that level's scale it is that level. The 24 degree take of the ring asset (untinted) adds only its detail finer than lowDeg degrees, which is under one texel of the level above. The fill gives way to the kept level over blendPx inside its edge. Where the take does not reach, the level above stands alone.

entire.how: A body of this field that the border of the skirt's sown field crosses is not cut there: it stays whole when at least half of it lies where this field stays, and goes whole otherwise. Read at half this field's raster; join and halo in px of that raster.

field.how: The far cloud of the place as bodies. Four generated top down pictures of a cumulus field over open sea (takes/field-t1..4.png, prompt-field.txt) are cut into cloud bodies. Alpha is the darkest channel between cloud[0] and the brightest value within rimPx (at least cloud[1]), so a rim beside bright cloud is a soft edge and a shaded flank is solid; a soft edge takes the colour of the bright cloud beside it (bleed: sigma px, power of the weight). glint: per take the half axes in px of an ellipse about the upper left corner where the take shows a sun glint; bodies with more than 0.3 of their area inside are dropped, and out to pale[0] times the ellipse the alpha limits rise to pale[1] and pale[2] so the pale sea is not taken for cloud. Bodies that touch the edge of a take are dropped. The cast shadow is the ratio of the sea to its lit level (shadow). Each take is turned so that its shadows run along the shadow of the Sun at the plate centre, reduced by scale, and used as it is and mirrored about that line. The bodies are laid on a raster of widthDeg about the plate centre, once per entry of sizes (the reduction of the takes and the share of the density that size takes: share[0] where the density is under share[2], share[1] where it is over share[3]), on a jittered grid of step tile widths; a body stays with the chance (density times share) to the power. A body whose bright tenth stays under veil.bright (the darkest channel at veil.tenth of its solid part, in code values of the take) is a veil or a cloud in the shade of another: it stays only where the density is over veil.dense, among lit bodies, because alone on the sea it reads as a flat grey patch (in the four takes these bodies are 8 to 10 percent of the cloud area and 48 to 77 percent of the bodies by count). Every kept body is also trimmed to its cloud. A core is a connected part of the solid matte that is bright (darkest channel from veil.bright) and opaque (matte from veil.alpha[1]). Within veil.reach[0] times the square root of a core's area a pixel stays whole (cores are counted in size classes of 4, 8, 16 px and so on, a pixel takes the nearest core of each class by that class's size); from veil.reach[1] it stays by its matte alone: none where the matte, blurred over veil.sigmaPx px, is under veil.alpha[0], whole from veil.alpha[1]. Measured on the four takes: 12 to 15 percent of the solid matte goes, 0.03 to 2.2 percent of the pixels whose darkest channel is over 170, and 31 to 37 percent of the lit bodies of 20 to 300 px lose over half of their pixels. What goes is the pale sea that a take shows between its clouds and the thin cell deck of take 4, which the matte takes for cloud at a share of about 0.4 to 0.65 and which read as flat grey sheets beside the white clouds of the field (frame 1889); an opaque flank of a tower stays. The density is described in density.how. A body takes the take's shadow along the line from it down the Sun's way (reachPx), in the share that kept bodies have among all bodies standing up Sun of the point: both are counted along the Sun's line between span[0] and span[1] times the take's measured shadow offset (measured on take 3 at scale 0.7: the shadows of bodies of 1600 to 6400 px lie between 0.55 and 1.4 of the offset, those of larger bodies between 0.3 and 2), and the bodies dropped at a take's edge or in its glint count as not kept. Where every body is kept the shadows are the take's own; a thin field shows no shadow without its cloud. Shadows fall on the ground and, by onCloud, on bodies laid before. levels.py lays the field over every level and the plate: under it the plate gives way to the hold's own levels (12 degrees where that reaches, 24 beyond, calmed, through seaGain) by the density and by the far ramp of the block far, so the repaint of the far zone with its soft cloud and its dotted land is not used, the ground takes the shadows, and the bodies take white, the per channel ratio of the bright cloud (darkest channel over white.bright) of the lay back within white.nearDeg of the point under the twin camera to the bright cloud of the field, kept inside white.limit. In the low plate the lay back keeps its tones and takes the detail of the field: what the plate with the field differs by from its own blur over low.sigmaDeg, where the blurred alpha passes low.alpha and the lay back is cloud (low.cloud).

density.how: Where the bodies lie, on size px over widthDeg. The bodies stand on the specks of the hold's own cloud layer (speck), so on the way down a speck of the map grows into a body at the same coordinates and none is born beside it. Specks are taken out where the ground the close image covers (the lay back, its edge softened by edgeDeg) lies nearer than far degrees of arc from the point under the twin camera (the near limit of far pushed outward by farVary: sigma in degrees and reach in degrees of a seeded noise), where the approved picture's own clouds stand, and toward the rim of the raster over wide.edgeDeg (wide.edgeVary degrees of a seeded noise). ring.calmDeg, ring.plate and ring.wipe are the calm ring levels.py reads: where the field lies near the plate's own clouds the plate's sea is calmed under it. vary (sigma in degrees, strength) varies the calm ring's width.

speck.how: The bodies stand on the specks of the map, and the cover is kept. deck.py reads the cover of the hold's own cloud layer (file, of the full set) on the field's raster and spreads it over deg degrees of arc (about the layer's own texel). Where that passes alpha[0] to alpha[1] the ground is speck; the spread cover itself is the cover wanted there. lay places the tiles as before but keeps a body by the cover still lacking: the cover wanted less the cover laid so far, both spread over nearDeg degrees, over the tile's own cover, is the chance that a body of the tile is kept (times the old shaping by size for the three sizes; after them the smallest size is laid fill times more with no shaping, to take up what is left), and a body is kept only if more than onBody of it stands on speck. So a speck of the map grows into bodies at the same coordinates, none is born on open sea, and the light of a patch (its cloud share times the cloud's light plus the rest times the sea's) is the hold's. rings are the bands, in degrees of arc from the point under the twin camera, deck.py prints the cover wanted and laid by. wedge: the cover the hold shows over the ground the close camera sees (place.json plates.wedge, the fourth value of its file) is laid over the layer's cover first, so the bodies of that ground stand on the specks the hold shows there.

sea.how: The sea the close camera looks across carries bodies as main's levels carry puffs there (MAIL 1537, ruling (i)). seacover.py reads the levels of levels degrees as commit ships them and as the hold's commit (place.json plates.holdCommit) ships them, the finer over the wider with the globe's feather, on size px over a square of widthDeg degrees on the plate's plane. Their cloud is where their level is brighter than the hold's on the darkest channel, through rise, so a whole body counts and not its brightest part alone; the hold's own cloud is the darkest channel through cloud and not warmer than warm (red less blue), the rule of the standing field. Each tree's levels are laid on the raster by their own windows first: the hold's commit ships plain windows about the spot, today's level of 24 degrees is a window of a wider raster with an offset, so the two do not match px for px as files. Kept is their cloud where the hold has no cloud of its own (own, after a blur of ownDeg degrees), over sea (sea on the hold's level: blue over red by sea[0] code values and no further under green than sea[1]; what is not sea, blurred over landDeg degrees, through land), from arcDeg degrees of arc from the point under the close camera outward, inside the turn the close camera's frame spans (sidePx px of that frame past each side, soft), and standDeg degrees inside the rim of the standing field (place.json plates.stand), so every body laid here stands. The file holds that cover and, as its second value, the sea (one less the step of land). deck.py lays the field as before and then, with a generator of its own (seed), lays bodies for this cover alone: a body is kept where more than onBody of it stands within roomDeg degrees of that cover (edge soft over softDeg), by the cover still lacking as in the fill, passes times for each size of scales; the cover wanted is amount times the kept cover, and a body with more than onLand of itself over what is not sea is dropped. So the rest of the field stays as it was to the texel and bodies stand there in about that amount; the hold's cloud layer does not carry it, so the hold reads as before and these bodies come with the levels alone. Order: seacover.py, deck.py, levels.py, band.py, above.py.

calm.how: The land of the hold's 12, 24 and 48 degree levels and of the plate carries a regular pattern of pale dots that reads as lights by day. Land is where green or pale ground stands near (green: code values the green channel must lead by; pale: what red and green must lead blue by; sigmaPx, reachPx, share) and the ground is warmer than the sea (warm), away from cloud (cloud: the darkest channel over the first value with red no more than the second above blue, where that stands wider than the disc below, widened by cloudPx). There the picture is its opening by a disc of dotPx radius (per level width in degrees; a level not named stays as it is), which takes away bright marks narrower than the disc and keeps every dark one, then its median over median times that radius (never brighter than the picture was) blurred by softPx, plus keep of what the opening took away. The plate keeps its land as it is only where the lay back covers it inside the window of the fine level, which carries the detail of the close view there; that window gives way to the calm over fineFadeDeg from its edge inward. Land under haze in the plate is bluer than the rule for the levels allows (measured on the land north of the place: blue leads green by -14 to 15 there, by 20 and more over the sea), so the plate has its own values in the block plate: blue is what green must lead blue by where no channel is over top (bright ground bluer than the first rule is the glint or the flank of a cloud, not land), warm as above.

wipe.how: Marks of the repaint in the plate, painted over from their surround (inpainting, Telea, radius 5): x, y and radius in px of the 4096 plate. Inside reach times the radius everything brighter than bright (darkest channel, code values) is taken, grown by growPx, so the whole mark goes and the fill starts from the sea round it.

glint.how: The glint of the plate, measured for the globe: warm bright sea (red over red, red less blue inside warm, blue over blue) at 1 over scale of the plate, blurred by blurPx, the largest blob; its centre and second moments go to plates.glint in place.json.

calm.how: The glint's light and the calm sea under it (plates.glint.calm in place.json), worked out at work px for the window, for the views that are not in the glint's direction. The calm sea is the open sea (lowest channel under white, blue less red over blue, deep: the share of the top channel that is colour) blurred by seaDeg degrees counting open sea only. Lit water is no cloud (cloud and warm of place.json), redder than the calm sea by lit (code values of 255) and adds as much red as green (glow of place.json), so reefs stay. The light is the lit water blurred by lightDeg degrees less the calm sea, where have of that window is lit, inside the reach (degrees from the glint's centre, none from reachDeg[0], full within reachDeg[1]; none at the window edge over edge of the width).

veil.how: The veil of the low plate (place.json plates.low.veil) carries the haze of the lay back on past the lay back. Inside the lay back's cover it is the lay back less the plate. Outside it is the mean of that difference over rings of ringDeg degrees about the point under the close camera (profile.size px work raster, rings with at least minPx px of cover), held from holdFromDeg degrees at the mean of all cover beyond (blend over blendDeg). What the lay back has over that mean at its edge is carried outward and dies over about spreadDeg degrees, so the cover's edge is no line.

nearSea.how: The sea of the plate in the calm zone of field.density.ring (weight field-near.png through field.density.ring.wipe). The plate there is the hold's map or its repaint: the sea floor is drawn as relief and the cloud is soft and lit from above, which beside the close view reads as a map. In the zone the sea is its own mean over sigmaDeg degrees, taken over sea alone: not over cloud (grey: darkest channel over the brightest, bright: the darkest channel in code values, both must pass, widened by growDeg degrees) and not over land (calm.py with the plate's values, widened by landDeg degrees). Land stays as it is. The broad tone of the sea is kept, so nothing steps at the zone's edge; the field's bodies and their shadows are laid on after it.

rim.how: The outer limit of the calm zone. The zone ends where the plate's limit of deck.py ends it (field.density.ring.plate through the feather of the plates and field.density.ring.wipe): a square about the centre of the raster, four straight lines 23 px wide, which cut the plate's clouds, the drawn relief of its sea and its shadows where the rise looks at them from near. Here the weight of the zone is carried on past that line (its values carryDeg degrees inside the line are held outward) and ended anew: over open sea by a smooth step softDeg degrees to each side of the line, so the relief and the shadows come in with no border; near a cloud of the plate (the cloud of nearSea, widened by growDeg and smoothed by nearDeg degrees) by a step edgeDeg degrees to each side of a line that the cloud itself moves, by push degrees for one unit of its lumps (its brightness smoothed by the first of lumpDeg less the same smoothed by the second, in degrees), so a cloud ends on its own lumps and no cloud ends on a straight line. Nothing changes further from the line than softDeg, or than push times the largest lump plus edgeDeg where a cloud moves the line further (0.4 degrees is not reached on this plate).

skirt.how: The ground round the canvas on the plate. The lay back ends at the canvas's rim (the frame of the close picture laid on the ground); outside it the plate was bare calm sea out to the hold's own sea, so the dive showed the canvas by its outline. Here the same kind of ground goes on past the rim, made of the canvas's own bodies and of nothing else. Bodies: inside the boxes of bodies.from (px of the plate, open sea of the canvas, clear of the glint and of land) a cloud is what stands over the sea's own local tone (bodies.cloud, code values of light over the mean of the sea alone within sigmaDeg degrees) and a shadow is sea darker than that tone (bodies.shade, share of the tone, smoothed over smoothPx px). Cloud and shadow that touch within joinPx[0] px are one body, and those that touch within joinPx[1] px are one group; a body is kept from areaPx[0] px, a group from areaPx[1] px, none over areaPx[2] px, none that the box or the rim cuts, none with less than cloudPx px of cloud. The lit rim of a flat cloud is no body: a cover is left out when more than curl[2] of it lies in long thin parts (a connected part of more than curl[1] px whose area is over curl[0] times the round that fits in it). A body carries the cloud's own colour and cover and the shadow as the share of light it leaves (never over 1), with a soft border of marginPx px. Field: bodies are laid outside the rim by a seeded draw (seed), whole, never across the rim (nearest fromDeg degrees), never on land, never on each other (apartPx px apart). Where: at the rim as much cloud as the canvas has just inside it (the canvas's cloud by bodies.cloud, its mean over the canvas within rim.coverDeg degrees, taken at the nearest point of the rim and carried outward as the sea's tone is, times the body px that one px of cloud brings, in units of cover and at most rim.most of it), so a clump of the canvas at the rim goes on outside it and open water at the rim goes on as open water; over rim.overDeg degrees from the rim that gives way to the field's own draw, which is as dense as cover says, in clumps with open water between (a seeded smooth field of clumpDeg degrees through the step clump); thinning to none between fieldDeg[0] and fieldDeg[1] degrees from the rim and where the plate gives way to the hold (far.fromDeg). Which: a group with the chance groups, else a single body; choose of them are drawn, a body whose home sea has the tone s with the weight exp(-((s - t) / kindTone)^2) on a spot whose sea has the tone t, so the kind of cloud follows the sea it stands over and the tan tufts of the canvas's dark near edge go on over the dark sea outside it; of those drawn the one laid least so far is laid; no body nearer than twinDeg degrees to itself and a group at most again times. How: at a size between scale[0] and scale[1] of its own, as it is or mirrored about the line the shadows fall along, so every shadow keeps the canvas's own Sun (the direction is the Sun of plates.stand on the ground of the place). Light: the canvas's own law, measured on its bodies: the light of a cloud (the mean over its cover) against the tone of the sea it stands over (both as 0.114 B + 0.587 G + 0.299 R) is fitted by one straight line; a body laid outside the rim is lit as that line says for the sea's tone on its spot, against the same for its home, so the dim clouds of the picture's dark near edge go on as dim clouds over the dark sea outside it; the gain stays within gain. Shadows darken the sea under them by their own share, the darkest where two meet. Under the field the sea is its tone alone: between the rim (whole from calmDeg degrees outside it) and fieldDeg the hold's own soft cloud, its shoals and its drawn relief give way to the wanted tone, since a body of another kind beside the canvas's own shows the border. A cloud of the map gives way whole or stays whole, never in part (whole): the lit cloud of nearSea, joined within whole.join px, is one cloud; one that reaches into the canvas stays (the rim does not cut a cloud), any other goes when the mean of the weight over it is a half or more and stays else, with its soft border of whole.halo px; no body of the field is laid on a cloud that stays. Land stays, and land here is green land alone (green: code values of green over red and over blue, widened by landDeg), because the land of calm.py also takes pale shoals and soft cloud for land. The field of deck.py is taken off by the same weight. Inside the canvas the plate keeps its pixels. Tone: one law for the open sea outside the canvas. At the rim the sea has the tone the plate's sea has just inside the rim (its mean over open sea alone: not over the lit cloud, not over what stands over the local tone as a cloud of bodies.cloud does and not over green land; shadow and the picture's own dark near edge count, since the tone outside has to be the tone the rim has; within rimDeg degrees, and where that little of open sea is left the mean within sigmaDeg degrees fills in with the weight fill, so a cloud at the rim does not throw its light outward as a pale wedge; carried outward from the nearest point of the rim and smoothed over carryDeg degrees among the points outside the rim alone, so the brighter sea further inside does not lift the tone at the rim), and it runs out into the tone of the hold's own sea as the plate shows it unveiled (the hold times seaGain, mean over sea alone within sigmaDeg degrees) by the smooth step of the distance from the rim over toneDeg degrees. A sea texel is moved from its own local tone to that tone as (value + soft) (wanted + soft) / (own + soft) - soft, so ripple, relief and shadows keep their depth in proportion; cloud (grey, bright of nearSea) and land keep their values. No round about the point under the close camera is left: the only line the tone knows is the rim, and there both sides are equal.

whole.how: A cloud of the map outside the canvas is one body (lit px joined over join px): it stays whole where under half of it lies where the field takes over and goes whole otherwise, with halo px round it. A body that the canvas's rim cuts goes whole: it has at least least lit px within touch px of the rim and at fewer than half of those px a lit body of the canvas within meet px on the other side, so the canvas shows sea where the body's other part lay and the rim would be its straight side. A body that goes on into a cloud of the canvas is one with it and is judged as the others.

toRim.how: The generated top view (q12-g) holds the canvas's own texels only on a part of the canvas: its near field, cut by a straight line some way inside the canvas's south rim and ending a little inside its near rim. Between that part and the rim the generated view painted a sea of its own, so the plate showed the canvas's end as a line inside the canvas and the close ground then arrived over another picture there. Here the plate holds the canvas out to its rim: where the plate (after the wipe of the repaint's marks) and the lay back (q12-lay) are the same picture (largest absolute difference of a channel, mean over sigmaDeg degrees inside the canvas, under apart code values; the largest connected part) the canvas is held; from there the lay back goes on to the canvas's rim wherever the rim is nearer than reachDeg degrees to the held part and to the point (so only on the near and south side, not out over the hold's own ground to the west and north, where the canvas runs to the horizon), with a soft end of edgeDeg degrees. Where the plate holds the canvas so, the calm leaves the canvas's land as it is (before, only inside the window of the fine level, which cut the canvas's island at the window's edge). On the strip the canvas so gains, the plate does not give way to the hold (field.density) and is not calmed as near sea (nearSea), which both were drawn for the generated sea that stood there. A law on the ground alone. Land is a body too: where land of the picture the plate shows without the canvas (the generated view, and the hold's map where the plate gives way to it by field.density and far) lies across the canvas's rim (a connected part of that land, read as the calm reads land, with at least land.least px outside the canvas and as many inside it off the held part), the canvas has sea where the globe and the hold show that land, and the lay back laid to the rim cut the island or the shoal along the rim, a straight side in the sea. There the plate keeps that picture of the land, which ends inside the rim on a soft shore: the lay back gives way to it over land.reachDeg degrees round the land (the weight shown, which also says where the plate does not give way to the hold and is not calmed, is taken off there, so that land is treated as before this law). shown is the soft weight of the held part and the gained strip together, sharp at the rim itself.
